methods.formula: 10-year Monte Carlo: revenue growth switches between high / steady / decline regimes by a Markov chain; margin drifts by regime; value = Σ discounted FCFF − SBC + terminal, per share

methods.formula: FCFF = EBIT × (1 − t) + D&A − capex − ΔWC;  EV = Σ FCFF/(1+WACC)^t + TV/(1+WACC)^5;  TV = NOPAT₆ × (1 − g ÷ ROIC) ÷ (WACC − g);  value = (EV − debt + cash − claims) ÷ shares
steps: growth by year 40%, 32%, 25%, 18%, 10%; EBIT margin 4.3%; D&A 1.9% of revenue; capex 0.0% of revenue; ΔWC 10% of each revenue increase

methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $3.03B (to $4.54B) × margin 4.3% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $1.75B
K = capital to build it: $3.03B ÷ sales-to-capital 5.13 = $589.9M
σ = 116% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $1.59B
assets in place = NOPAT $51.27M ÷ WACC = $827.1M; value = ($827.1M + $1.59B − net debt $553.2M) ÷ 13,968,004 = $133.41
